 News Flash
 What Burlington County Voters Should Know Before Going to the Polls on Election Day
 Home - County News
 Posted on October 30, 2026 
 Election Day is almost here, and Burlington County polling places are expected to be busy.
 Early voting has already started and will remain available through Sunday, November 1, but for Burlington County voters planning to vote on Election Day, November 3, here are a few helpful tips:
 Where to vote? 
 On Election Day, voters should report to their regular polling locations. Voters should check their sample ballot for their specific location, especially in Bordentown Township, Burlington Township, Eastampton, Evesham, Lumberton, Moorestown, North Hanover, Pemberton Township, Tabernacle, Westampton, Burlington City, and Willingboro, because voting districts or polling locations in those towns have changed.
 Voters can also look up their assigned polling location online at  https://voter.svrs.nj.gov/polling-place-search .
 When do polls open and close? 
 Polls open at 6 a.m. and remain open until 8 p.m. Voters in line by 8 p.m. can cast their vote, and polling places will remain open until the last voter in line at 8 p.m. has voted.
 Bring your sample ballot to the polls 
 Voters are reminded to bring their sample ballots to the polls during early voting and on Election Day for an easier check-in. 
 Each sample ballot includes a barcode printed next to the polling place address box, which can be scanned in the electronic poll books to help voters check in quickly and accurately. If a sample ballot doesn't scan properly, or the voter doesn’t bring one, they can still check in the traditional way with a poll worker.
 If a voter has any difficulty checking in at their polling place or their voter registration is incorrect in the poll book, they should contact the Superintendent of Elections Office at 609-265-5111. Voters should not leave their polling place without casting a provisional ballot and filling out an affidavit, which is used to verify the validity of a voter’s eligibility.
 Do not bring vote-by-mail ballots to the polls 
 Voters who received a vote-by-mail (VBM) ballot can submit them in one of three ways:
 • Placing them in one of Burlington County’s 29 secure drop boxes. The locations are available at  https://bit.ly/burlington-drop-boxes 
 • Hand-delivering them to the Board of Elections at 301 Harper Drive, Moorestown
 • Mailing them with the U.S. Postal Service
 Remember all completed VBM ballots must be placed in a drop box or delivered to the Election Board by 8 p.m. on November 3. Mail-returned ballots must be postmarked no later than November 3 and arrive at the Election Board on or before 6 days after Election Day.
 Voters who received or requested a VBM ballot for the General Election will only be permitted to vote at an early voting or Election Day polling location with a provisional ballot.
 Familiarize yourself with the voting equipment 
 Burlington County voters headed to the polls for the General Election are encouraged to watch an online video that explains how to use the County’s voting machines.
 The machines include touch-screen ballot-marking devices with printers and separate tabulator machines used to count ballots after they are printed.
 The video can be viewed at  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bvn4gF1msA4 .
 Disability assistance 
 Voters with disabilities and accessibility needs have rights at the polls. Accessible voting machines are available at every polling location, and voters can request reasonable accommodations from poll workers. Voters who need help are permitted to bring a family member or friend with them to assist, or they can ask a poll worker to help them. Employers and union representatives are not permitted to help.
 Voters who experience accessibility challenges at a polling location or have difficulty obtaining accommodations should call the Board of Elections at 609-265-5557.
 ‘I Voted’ stickers 
 Voters who cast their ballot in-person during the early voting period or on November 3 will receive an ‘I Voted’ sticker from the Burlington County Election Board as they leave their polling location. Voters who returned a vote-by-mail ballot will also be sent a postcard with an “I Voted” sticker.
 Leave your political attire and signs home 
 Electioneering is not permitted within 100 feet of any polling location. This restriction extends to wearing hats, clothing, pins, or other materials advocating for a particular candidate, as well as holding rallies, putting up posters, or carrying signs that attempt to influence voters.
 Residents with questions about the election, voting procedures, and regulations can call the Burlington County Elections hotline at 609-265-VOTE (8683).
